Collection was run twice tonight — a `--dry-run` first (758 candidates seen, 389
would have cleared the score bar), then the real run. A duplicate `--dry-run`
process, left over from an earlier command that had timed out client-side
without actually stopping, was found running concurrently with the real
collection and killed once noticed; nothing points at it having corrupted
anything, but it is why the collection log shows a stretch of Semantic
Scholar/dblp errors that a single run should not produce.

The queue was already at its 40-task cap before this run started, so only 6
papers were actually admitted as new records (the rest of the night's
candidates were rejected on score or skipped past the cap, not queued) —
`summaries_unread` sat at 245, which is the size of the real backlog, cap or
no cap.

**The full 40-task queue was then drained.** Six had an attached PDF and were
read as documents; one more (`arxiv:2605.17626`) had none until a
`pipelines.backfill` pass fetched it, after which it read as a document too.
The other 33 were ACL Anthology / curated-list entries with no PDF the
collector could reach; fifteen of those also carried an empty abstract in the
payload (all ICLR 2026 poster listings, matching the run problem above) and
were completed by fetching the paper's own ICLR virtual-site page rather than
guessing from the title — still recorded as `read_from: abstract`, since a
conference page is not the paper itself. Two papers turned out to be
essentially off-topic for this archive (a training-time early-stopping
generalization-theory paper and a robot-manipulation compute-scaling paper),
matched only by a keyword shared with the topic's vocabulary; their
`relevance` fields say so plainly rather than forcing a fit.

Rendering the drained queue folded 40 papers in, grew the wiki from 2,378 to
2,656 entities and 247 to 258 notes, and — because the queue had room again —
immediately refilled it: 27 papers that had been sitting past the cap all
night, plus 13 concept-definition tasks for entities that just crossed the
promotion threshold on this batch's evidence. Neither was drained this
session; 205 papers remain unread in total.
